page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.32-128 is a compute-focused flexible virtual machine configured with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs across an x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7J13 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz, the system is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, necessitating reliance on remote block storage volumes for persistent data management. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant scaling in highly parallel environments. In multi-core stress testing, the instance scores 85,507.98 on stress-ng, placing it within the top quartile of tested configurations. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 283.39 GB/sec, also ranking in the top 25%. Cached memory read throughput is strong at 4,137.26 GB/sec for small blocks, whereas uncached large-block throughput settles into the mid-tier with 118.61 GB/sec read and 60.7 GB/sec write. Single-threaded metrics, including single-core stress-ng (2,675.28) and single-threaded gzip compression (25.42 GB/sec), perform within average thresholds.

With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, VM.Standard.E4.Flex.32-128 offers high compute density per gigabyte of memory, yielding favorable cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads that do not demand extensive RAM footprints. It is best suited for parallel batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed web serving, and CPU-based lightweight model inference.
